anomalies.observed: T3 (AON6407, P-channel MOSFET) has its source (pin 2) connected to /+24V_F (the fused input from the 24V supply) and its drain (pin 3) connected to +24V (the main board rail).
anomalies.expected: For a P-channel MOSFET used as high-side reverse-polarity protection, the drain should be on the input side and the source on the output side, so that the body diode is reverse-biased under reverse input polarity and blocks current.
anomalies.impact: Reverse polarity protection is defeated. If the 24V input is connected backwards, T3's body diode (anode at drain, cathode at source) becomes forward-biased, conducting current from the +24V rail to the reversed input and exposing the regulator, drivers, and other components to reverse voltage.

parsed.summary: The design files contain an anomaly: the P-channel reverse-polarity protection MOSFET T3 has its source and drain swapped, so it will not block a reversed 24V input and could allow damaging reverse current into the board.
